mortensor: flexible mortality forecasting across data granularities

Source: R/mortensor-package.R
mortensor-package.Rd

The package is organised in layers:

Details

  • Data: mt_data() stores deaths, exposures and populations observed at any age and period resolution (age_groups(), single_ages(), single_years(), parse_age_labels()); as_mt_data() and mt_from_hmd() read Human Mortality Database data; mt_validate() checks plausibility; mt_example() simulates data with known truth.

  • Harmonisation: mt_regroup() aggregates exactly, mt_ungroup() estimates single-year data with the penalized composite link model, mt_smooth() smooths rates; mt_prep() bundles these steps so that backtests refit them on every training window.

  • Models: rwd(), lee_carter(), arima_series(), ets_series(), hyndman_ullah(), coherent_fdm(), stmomo(), stanmomo(), li_lee(), coda(), apc_bayes() (package bamp), the experimental tucker3() and coda_causes(), and ensemble(), fitted with mt_fit() (optionally tuned with tuned()) and forecast with mt_forecast() as simulated paths (mt_draws). product_ratio() and cause_shares() are deprecated. The article "Methods and sources" lists the published source of every method.

  • Hierarchies: mt_hierarchy() describes crossed or nested strata (for example sex x region x deprivation quintile with their totals), mt_aggregate_strata() adds the aggregates, mt_reconcile() and reconciled() make forecasts add up draw by draw, mt_order_strata() imposes orderings.

  • Wrappers for any model: ensemble(), reconciled(), recalibrated() (spread fitted to recent forecast errors), anchored() (jump-off at the observed level), bootstrapped() and tuned().

  • Evaluation: mt_backtest() and mt_score(), for rates, life expectancy and age-standardised rates.

  • The past: mt_observed(), mt_contrast() and mt_inequality().

  • Derived quantities and plots: life_table(), life_expectancy(), mt_deaths(), mt_plot_forecast() and the other mt_plot_*() functions.

  • Decomposition: mt_decompose() splits differences in life expectancy and other summaries by age, cause and subgroup composition, for observed data, forecasts or both.

Caution

mortensor is experimental software written largely with AI coding assistants ("vibe-coded"). It has unit tests and a validation pipeline, but it has not been peer reviewed and its interfaces still change. Use it at your own risk and check results independently before using them in publications, reports or decisions.
